nodes.summary: If $C$ is a linear code of length $n$ over a finite field $F$, then exactly $|F|^{\dim C}$ of the $|F|^n$ words of length $n$ lie in $C$, where $\dim C$ is the dimension of $C$ over $F$.
nodes.title: Number of codewords of a linear code

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $\iota$ a finite set. The dot product form is the bilinear form on $F^\iota$ that sends a pair of words $(x, y)$ to $x \cdot y = \sum_{i \in \iota} x_i y_i$.
nodes.title: Dot product bilinear form

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a matrix over a field $F$ with finitely many rows and finitely many columns. Then the dual of the code generated by $G$ (the span of its rows) is the code with parity-check matrix $G$ (the words $x$ with $Gx = 0$).
nodes.title: Dual of the code generated by a matrix

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a matrix over a field $F$ with finitely many rows and finitely many columns. Then the dual of the code with parity-check matrix $H$ (the words $x$ with $Hx = 0$) is the code generated by $H$ (the span of its rows).
nodes.title: Dual of the code with a given parity-check matrix

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $\iota$ a finite set. The dual $C^\perp$ of a linear code $C \subseteq F^\iota$ is the linear code of all words $x \in F^\iota$ with $x \cdot c = \sum_{i \in \iota} x_i c_i = 0$ for every codeword $c \in C$.
nodes.title: Dual code

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, $\kappa$ a finite set and $A$ a $\kappa \times \rho$ matrix over $F$. For the systematic generator matrix $G = [I \mid A]$, whose columns are indexed by the disjoint union $\kappa \sqcup \rho$, the encoding $mG$ of every message $m \in F^\kappa$ agrees with $m$ on the coordinates in $\kappa$: $(mG)_i = m_i$ for every $i \in \kappa$.
nodes.title: The systematic encoder copies the message

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a $\kappa \times \iota$ matrix over a field $F$, with $\kappa$ finite. The encoder of $G$ sends a message $m \in F^\kappa$ to the word $mG \in F^\iota$ given by $(mG)_j = \sum_{k \in \kappa} m_k G_{kj}$, the combination of the rows of $G$ with coefficients $m$.
nodes.title: Encoder of a generator matrix

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a matrix over a field $F$ whose columns are indexed by a finite set. For every natural number $t$ there is a syndrome table for $H$ that is correct up to radius $t$.
nodes.title: Existence of correct syndrome tables

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $\iota$ a finite set. For every linear code $C \subseteq F^\iota$, $\dim C + \dim C^\perp = |\iota|$, where $C^\perp$ is the dual code.
nodes.title: Dimension of the dual code

nodes.summary: Let $C$ be a linear code of length $n$ over a finite field $F$, and let $d \le n$ be a natural number that is at most the minimum distance of $C$. Then $\dim C + d \le n + 1$.
nodes.title: Singleton bound for linear codes, dimension form

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $\iota$ a finite set. For all words $x, y \in F^\iota$, the Hamming distance between $x$ and $y$ (the number of coordinates where they differ) equals the Hamming weight of $x - y$ (its number of nonzero coordinates).
nodes.title: Hamming distance is the weight of the difference

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a $\rho \times \iota$ matrix over a field $F$, with $\iota$ finite, and let $t$ be a natural number. A syndrome table for $H$, that is, a map $T$ from syndromes $s \in F^\rho$ to error patterns $T(s) \in F^\iota$, is correct up to radius $t$ when, for every word $e \in F^\iota$ of Hamming weight at most $t$, the word $T(He)$ has the same syndrome as $e$, that is $H \, T(He) = He$, and has Hamming weight…
nodes.title: Syndrome table correct up to a radius

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field and $\iota$ an index set, not necessarily finite. A linear code over $F$ with coordinates indexed by $\iota$ is an $F$-linear subspace of the space of words, the functions $\iota \to F$.
nodes.title: Linear code

nodes.summary: For a linear code of finite length over a field, the minimum distance equals the minimum weight.
nodes.title: Minimum distance equals minimum weight

nodes.summary: If $C$ is a linear code of length $n$ over a field and $C$ is not the zero subspace, then the minimum distance of $C$ is finite and at most $n$.
nodes.title: Minimum distance is at most the length

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field and $C$ a linear code of length $n$ and dimension $k$ over $F$ that is not the zero subspace. Then the minimum distance of $C$ is at most $n - k + 1$.
nodes.title: Singleton bound for linear codes

nodes.summary: The minimum distance of a linear code $C$ of finite length is the least Hamming distance (number of coordinates where they differ) between two distinct codewords of $C$, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$; it is $\infty$ if $C$ has at most one codeword.
nodes.title: Minimum distance

nodes.summary: The minimum weight of a linear code $C$ of finite length is the least weight of a nonzero codeword of $C$, where the weight of a word is its number of nonzero coordinates; it is taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ and is $\infty$ if $C$ has no nonzero codeword.
nodes.title: Minimum weight

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, $\kappa$ and $\iota$ finite index sets and $\rho$ any index set, and let $G$ be a $\kappa \times \iota$ matrix and $H$ a $\rho \times \iota$ matrix over $F$. The code generated by $G$ equals the code with parity-check matrix $H$ if and only if $G H^{\mathsf{T}} = 0$ and $\operatorname{rank} G + \operatorname{rank} H$ equals $|\iota|$, the length of the code.
nodes.title: Generator/parity-check duality

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, $\kappa$ a finite index set, $\iota$ any index set and $G$ a $\kappa \times \iota$ matrix over $F$. The code generated by $G$ is the linear code of all words $m G$ with $m : \kappa \to F$, the image of the encoder $m \mapsto m G$; equivalently, the span of the rows of $G$.
nodes.title: Code generated by a matrix

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, $\iota$ a finite index set, $\rho$ any index set and $H$ a $\rho \times \iota$ matrix over $F$. The code with parity-check matrix $H$ is the linear code of all words $c : \iota \to F$ whose syndrome $H c$ is zero, that is, the kernel of $c \mapsto H c$.
nodes.title: Code with a given parity-check matrix

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a finite field with $q$ elements and $C$ a linear code of length $n$ and dimension $k$ over $F$. If $t$ is a natural number such that $2t$ is less than the minimum distance of $C$, then
nodes.title: Hamming bound for linear codes

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, $\iota$ and $\rho$ finite sets, $H$ a $\rho \times \iota$ parity-check matrix over $F$, and $t \in \mathbb{N}$, where the words $F^\iota$ come with a fixed enumeration. The search table sends a syndrome $s \in F^\rho$ to the first word $e \in F^\iota$ in the enumeration with Hamming weight at most $t$ and syndrome $He = s$, and to $0$ if there is no such word.
nodes.title: Syndrome table by exhaustive search

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, $\iota$ a finite set and $H$ a parity-check matrix over $F$ with columns indexed by $\iota$. If $c \in F^\iota$ is a codeword of the code with parity-check matrix $H$ and $e \in F^\iota$ is any word, then the received word $c + e$ has the same syndrome as $e$, that is, $H(c + e) = He$.
nodes.title: The syndrome depends only on the error

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a parity-check matrix over a field $F$, let $C$ be the code with parity-check matrix $H$, let $d \in \mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$ be its minimum distance, and let $t \in \mathbb{N}$ with $2t < d$. If a syndrome table is correct up to radius $t$ for $H$, then for every codeword $c \in C$ and every word $e$ of Hamming weight at most $t$, syndrome decoding with this table sends the received word $c + e$ to…
nodes.title: Syndrome decoding corrects every error of weight at most $t$

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a parity-check matrix over a field $F$ such that the code $C$ with parity-check matrix $H$ has finite minimum distance $d$, and let $t = \lfloor (d - 1)/2 \rfloor$. If a syndrome table is correct up to radius $t$ for $H$, then for every codeword $c \in C$ and every word $e$ of Hamming weight at most $t$, syndrome decoding with this table sends the received word $c + e$ to $c$.
nodes.title: Syndrome decoding up to half the minimum distance

nodes.summary: Syndrome decoding with a lookup `table` from syndromes to error patterns: subtract the error pattern the table assigns to the syndrome of the received word.
nodes.title: Syndrome decoding

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, $\iota$ a finite set and $\rho$ a set. For a matrix $H \in F^{\rho \times \iota}$ (a parity-check matrix) and a word $y \in F^\iota$, the syndrome of $y$ is the vector $Hy \in F^\rho$.
nodes.title: Syndrome

nodes.summary: Let $F$ be a field, $\kappa$ and $\rho$ finite sets, and $A$ a $\kappa \times \rho$ matrix over $F$. Then the code generated by $G = [I_\kappa \mid A]$ equals the code with parity-check matrix $H = [-A^{\mathsf{T}} \mid I_\rho]$, both being codes whose coordinates are indexed by the disjoint union of $\kappa$ and $\rho$.
nodes.title: Systematic generator and parity-check matrices

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
